title: Incident coda: tenant QoS safety net and auto-calibration
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Post-incident follow-up from the 2026-02-28 dedicated cluster capacity degradation. Multiple tenants experienced elevated tail latency and partial evictions when a single tenant shifted workload shape (long beam search > short responses). Initial mitigation (manual reservation bump and short-term burst cap) restored service, but root cause analysis shows two systemic gaps: (1) reservation sizing is only computed from 30-day average token throughput, which misses sudden distribution shifts; (2) burst policy permits uncontrolled short-term consumption without early signaling, allowing a single tenant to consume ephemeral capacity and increase kernel contention across shared nodes.

Root cause (short):
- Reservation estimator insensitive to mode changes (search vs. streaming) and sequence length distribution.
- No fast-path isolation when cross-tenant kernel contention spikes; existing noisy-tenant detector only reacts after eviction thresholds are hit.
- Telemetry lacked a simple signal combining per-tenant KV cache miss rate + per-request kernel sched delay, which would have given an early warning.

Goal of this ticket:
- Deliver a "QoS safety net" composed of three coordinated subsystems: (A) signal validator pipeline to surface early cross-tenant contention signals, (B) an auto-calibrator that recommends (and can opt-in to apply) temporary reservation deltas based on recent distribution shifts, and (C) a burst-dampening controller that enforces soft limits and graceful degradation before hard evictions.

Why this is different from prior work:
- Existing playbooks focus on manual rightsizing and eviction reaction. This work aims for proactive, automated controls with clear observability and an auditable rollback path. We prioritize low-latency detection (seconds-to-minutes) and smooth degradation rather than immediate hard throttles.

High-level design:
1) Signal validator: lightweight aggregator that computes per-tenant metrics every 30s: sequence-length PMF delta, KV cache miss rate, kernel-sched-ms p50/p95. Emits "contention_score" and history window to console.
2) Auto-calibrator: rules engine using the validator signals + policy (customer tier, SLA) to propose reservation adjustments and label them as temporary (TTL 1h). Proposals are recorded in audit log and surfaced in Console with a one-click apply.
3) Burst-dampening controller: when contention_score crosses threshold for >2 consecutive windows, apply incremental soft-burst caps (token/sec) plus preferential routing offload for best-effort tenants. Soft caps degrade tail latency, not throughput for pinned reservations.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (this ticket): implement validator + dashboard and alerting (non-blocking). Ship to dedicated clusters in staging.
- Phase 1: implement auto-calibrator proposals (read-only) and Console UI for operator approval. Deploy canary on 2 small clusters.
- Phase 2: implement opt-in auto-apply logic with emergency rollback and conservative defaults. Start with internal customers.
- Phase 3: default-on for new clusters after 4 weeks of stable telemetry, migrate existing clusters with customer notifications.

Monitoring and SLOs:
- New metric: contention_score (0-100). Acceptance if mean contention_score drop >= 40% during similar incidents.
- Reduce customer-visible tail latency (p99 generation) by >30% in controlled replay tests.
- No unintended eviction events caused by auto-calibrator during staged rollouts.

Safety and audit:
- All auto-calibrator actions must be auditable, with a TTL and an explainable rationale string.
- Emergency kill-switch exposed in Console and an API endpoint to disable auto-apply for a cluster.

Acceptance criteria:
- Signal validator deployed to staging and producing stable contention_score with <= 10s processing latency.
- Console dashboard displays recent signals and a historical heatmap.
- Auto-calibrator produces actionable reservation proposals in staging for at least 4 distinct synthetic workload shifts.
- Burst-dampening controller applied in canary reduces kernel-sched-ms p95 by >= 25% in replay tests and does not trigger evictions.
- Runbook updated, and on-call trained for new alerts.

Docs and artifacts:
- Postmortem: https://confluence.internal.redwood/inference/postmortems/2026-02-28-dedicated-capacity
- Design sketch (signal schema + thresholds): https://drive.redwood.com/designs/tenant-qos-safety-net.pdf
- Reproduction script for load replay: https://github.com/redwood-inference/load-replay/tree/incident-2026-02
